scenes.text: Your boat just hit a reef. And it's sinking. Fast.
You were sailing alone, like you do every year on this day.
You grab what you can, and swim for the only thing you can see.
A tiny island. Nothing else for miles.
Here's what you saved. A knife. A tarp. Water. And the boat's emergency beacon.
Water first. Dig a hole, cup in the middle, tarp on top. The sun pulls water out of the sand.
Then shelter. Palm fronds on a frame, off the ground, away from the crabs.
Fire, with a bow drill. Forty minutes of sawing, and then, smoke.
Then the beacon. Switch it on, and it sends your location to rescuers. Help is coming.
That night, you fall asleep by the fire.
In the morning, you go to check the beacon.
Someone switched it off. And in the sand, footprints. Not yours.
Someone on this island doesn't want you rescued. What do you do? Top comment decides part two.
